title: Safe-apply: add canary apply + metric gates (p95 latency, error rate) for Optimize config changes
author: Logan Wright
release_notes: Adds canary apply mode for Optimize config changes with metric-gated progression. Default gates use p95 latency and request error rate; authorized operators may override with justification (audited).
description: Context: Safe-apply/rollback needs a progressive delivery option so we can catch obvious regressions (latency spikes, elevated errors) before full rollout. This PR introduces canary apply support with metric gates for Optimize config changes. The control plane now supports an optional canary phase that applies the config to a bounded subset of traffic/replicas for a short observation window, queries telemetry for p95 latency + error rate deltas vs baseline, and either promotes or aborts. Default thresholds are defined per environment/tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and can be overridden only by authorized roles with an explicit justification + linked ticket; every gate evaluation and override is auditable. What’s included: (1) Rollout state machine additions: CANARY_PENDING -> CANARY_RUNNING -> CANARY_EVALUATING -> (PROMOTE|ABORT) -> FULL_APPLY; (2) Gate evaluation service that queries metrics using correlation_id + scope filters (customer/region/route/model) and compares a baseline window to a canary window; (3) Default thresholds and policy: p95 latency regression and error-rate regression gates, with environment-specific defaults and hard maximums (cannot be overridden beyond safety caps); (4) API surface: new request fields for safe-apply (canary.enabled, canary.duration, canary.traffic_fraction, gates.override_requested, override_reason, linked_ticket); (5) Audit events: canary_started, canary_gate_evaluated, canary_aborted, canary_promoted, canary_gate_override_requested/approved/denied (override emits who/why); (6) Observability: counters + timers for gate eval duration and decision outcomes, plus structured logs for post-incident forensics. Default gates (initial): p95 latency: abort if canary p95 exceeds baseline by > max(30ms, 10%) for Hosted and > max(50ms, 15%) for Dedicated/Private; error rate: abort if canary (5xx + timeouts) exceeds baseline by > 0.20% absolute (Hosted) or > 0.30% absolute (Dedicated/Private); both computed over 5m canary window vs 10m baseline window, requiring minimum sample size (requests >= 2k Hosted / 1k Dedicated / configurable for Private). Override policy (initial): requires optimize.config.apply + optimize.config.gates.override; must supply override_reason and linked_ticket; hard caps remain enforced (cannot override above 2x default thresholds); override is a second explicit API call to avoid accidental bypass (two-step). Notes/limitations: gate signals are currently p95+error only (no saturation/quality gates in this PR); Private deployments without centralized telemetry can run canary without gates (validator will warn, UI will require explicit acknowledgement); baseline selection uses the immediate pre-canary window only (no longer historical baselining). Follow-ups: hook in additional gates (GPU saturation, queue depth) behind feature flag; Console wizard wiring (separate PR); documentation + runbook updates (Kira/Elliot).

conversation: Paula Mendes (2025-01-15): Can we confirm the default thresholds align with SRE’s MTTR goals and don’t create constant false aborts for small traffic canaries? Also please document the sample-size minimums and what happens when they’re not met. Logan Wright (2025-01-15): Yep. Added explicit min-requests per tier and a ‘NO_DECISION’ outcome when underpowered; in that case we hold in CANARY_RUNNING and re-evaluate every 60s up to a max canary duration, then abort with reason=insufficient_data (audited). Jada Williams (2025-01-16): Rollout semantics question: if gate evaluation fails due to telemetry timeout, do we fail closed (abort) or fail open (promote)? For safety I’d prefer fail closed, but we need an operator escape hatch. Logan Wright (2025-01-16): Implemented fail-closed by default: telemetry errors -> abort with reason=telemetry_unavailable. Operators can request override via new endpoint; override is two-step and audited. Neha Kapoor (2025-01-16): Please add hard safety caps so people can’t override to something insane during an incident. Also ensure we emit a counter for override usage (we’ll alert on frequent overrides). Logan Wright (2025-01-17): Added safetyCaps.ts (2x default max) and metrics: config_canary_override_total{env,tier,reason}. Allison Grant (2025-01-17): We need consistent metric names/tags. Please use correlation_id and scope tags but avoid high-cardinality customer_id in timeseries labels. Put customer_id only in logs/audit. Logan Wright (2025-01-17): Updated metrics to tag only env,tier,region,route_id,model_id; customer_id stays in audit/log payloads. Caleb Johnson (2025-01-18): Gate math nit: you’re comparing raw p95 values; can we compute both absolute delta and relative delta and choose the larger? Otherwise low-latency routes will fail too easily on small absolute shifts. Logan Wright (2025-01-18): Good catch. Implemented max(abs_ms, rel_pct) check (as described in PR) and added tests for low-baseline scenarios. Paula Mendes (2025-01-19): Copy for ‘insufficient_data’ abort reason needs to be operator-friendly for Console. Can we standardize reasons now? Logan Wright (2025-01-19): Added enum-like string constants for abort reasons: latency_regression, error_regression, telemetry_unavailable, insufficient_data, operator_abort. Jada Williams (2025-01-20): LGTM with the safety cap + fail-closed approach. Please ensure follow-up task for adding saturation gates is tracked. Logan Wright (2025-01-20): Added follow-up in PM-412 notes + created ENG follow-up for saturation gates behind flag (not blocking this PR).
